BXL-2425-00027-v4.headline: Adopt the pure-and-simple motion tabled by Hasan Koyuncu (PS), moving to the day's order without debate, thereby shelving Clémentine Barzin's motivated motion calling for a dedicated Brussels antisemitism action plan.
BXL-2425-00027-v4.type: Motion (ordre du jour pur et simple)
BXL-2425-00027-v4.proposed_by: Hasan Koyuncu (PS); motivated motion it displaces: Clémentine Barzin (MR), filed 12 June 2025
BXL-2425-00027-v4.source_brief:
Following an interpellation by Clémentine Barzin (MR) to Secretary of State Nawal Ben Hamou on Brussels actions to combat antisemitism in light of the 2005 and 2023 resolutions, two competing motions were tabled. Barzin's motivated motion called for a specific Brussels antisemitism plan separate from the broader anti-racism framework; Koyuncu's pure-and-simple motion, which under parliamentary rules takes procedural priority, instead proposes to close the session without endorsing that call.

- **What triggered the debate:** cited incidents — antisemitic remarks and assaults at a university, a swastika on a Second World War resistance memorial, named individuals' faces and addresses posted on Brussels streets — prompted MR to argue that antisemitism requires a distinct, targeted response beyond the existing Brussels anti-racism plan.
- **The majority's counter-argument:** several groups argued that the Secretary of State had already demonstrated concrete action in committee, that a 2023 parliamentary resolution already addressed antisemitism specifically, and that a global cross-cutting anti-racism approach is more unifying than a motion focused on one form of discrimination.
- **Gaza and context:** some speakers linked the resurgence of antisemitic acts to the aftermath of 7 October 2023 and the Gaza war; others argued the same period has also seen rising Islamophobia and racist violence, citing incidents in Brussels, and called for a working group covering all forms of racism together.
- **The rub:** whether an explicit, standalone plan to fight antisemitism — with its historically specific roots and particular manifestations — is more effective and appropriate, or whether folding it into a universal anti-racism approach better serves solidarity and avoids selective indignation.
deep_facts: The interpellation was addressed by Mme Clémentine Barzin (MR) to Mme Nawal Ben Hamou, Secretary of State for Housing and Equal Opportunities, concerning actions to combat antisemitism in light of the 2005 and 2023 resolutions; a motivated motion was filed by Barzin on 12 June 2025 and a pure-and-simple motion by M. Hasan Koyuncu (PS) on 17 June 2025 (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

Under article 119.7 of the Brussels Parliament's rules of procedure, the pure-and-simple motion takes procedural priority over the motivated motion; by being adopted, it renders the motivated motion 'sans objet' (without effect), as confirmed by the president at the close of the vote (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

Mme Barzin cited specific recent incidents: antisemitic statements and physical aggression at a Brussels university; a swastika painted on a memorial plaque honouring three young Second World War resistance fighters; personal attacks naming individuals on social media; and posters affixed in Brussels streets displaying the faces, names and addresses of prominent Jewish personalities (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

Barzin's stated rationale for a dedicated plan: antisemitism shares characteristics with other racisms but has specific historical roots stretching back through centuries, including anti-Judaism in Christian tradition, the dissemination of conspiratorial narratives, and the 20th-century genocide; she argued these specificities justify a distinct response, not a dilution of the struggle into other battles (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

PS speaker Jamal Ikazban argued the Secretary of State had already demonstrated she was acting — citing a October 2023 resolution specifically targeting antisemitism already adopted by a large majority — and proposed a cross-party working group (excluding far right) to combat all forms of hatred, while noting other serious racist violence including an averted mosque attack in Molenbeek and violence against Muslim residents on 4 May (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

PTB questioned the political motivation behind the MR motion, noting MR had not voted for the October 2023 antisemitism resolution adopted by a large majority, and also citing MR for having equated criticism of Israeli state policy with antisemitism, which PTB argued was disputed by many Jewish organisations; PTB affirmed firm opposition to all antisemitism while supporting the pure-and-simple motion (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

DéFI (Joëlle Maison) argued antisemitism has its own specificity warranting targeted attention while simultaneously calling for a working group to develop parallel plans — one targeting antisemitism, one targeting Islamophobia and violence against Muslims — to address both surges linked to the Gaza conflict and broader conflicts being imported into Brussels society (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

N-VA (Gilles Verstraeten) voted against the pure-and-simple motion, arguing it should be possible to discuss specific forms of hatred and design targeted responses without importing every other issue into the same debate, and warning that the inability to have a calm, focused conversation about antisemitism is itself concerning (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

Les Engagés (Marie Cruysmans) voted for the pure-and-simple motion with one abstention, expressing firm condemnation of antisemitism and all racist acts but arguing the motivated motion would be more divisive than unifying in the current geopolitical context; Ecolo (Farida Tahar) and Groen (Emile Luhahi) also supported the pure-and-simple motion while reaffirming commitment to fighting antisemitism (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).

The baroness Regina Sluszny, a former hidden child from the Second World War, had addressed the plenary chamber in the days before the vote, an appearance referenced by Barzin in her statement as a reminder of where silence and inaction lead (CRI, 19 Jun 2025).
BXL-2425-00027-v4.deep_lectura:
**Analyst read** *(inference — not stated verbatim in the record)*

- The procedural mechanism (pure-and-simple motion displacing the motivated motion) means the majority did not need to argue the substantive case against Barzin's plan on its merits — voting for the simple motion is procedurally a non-decision, which is precisely why it is politically attractive for groups who do not want to be seen as opposing anti-antisemitism action but also do not want to endorse MR's framing.
- The 2023 resolution becomes the majority's shield: pointing to a text already adopted lets groups claim they have already acted specifically on antisemitism while declining to take up what MR frames as inadequate follow-through — the real dispute is over whether the 2023 resolution is being implemented, not over principle.
- The Gaza dimension runs just below the surface throughout: several speakers linked rising antisemitism explicitly to 7 October 2023 and the war, while others linked rising Islamophobia to the same events; the tension between condemning antisemitism specifically and insisting on parallel treatment of Islamophobia reflects the way the Middle East conflict maps onto the composition and sensitivities of the Brussels Parliament.
- Framing a standalone antisemitism plan as 'divisive' is the most revealing argument in the debate: it implies that in Brussels's specific demographic and political context, a motion that names one form of discrimination for a dedicated plan risks being read as taking a side in a broader conflict — which is itself a signal of how internationally freighted the local politics of antisemitism have become.
BXL-2425-00027-v4.raw_fr: La séance plénière du 19 juin 2025 a été saisie de deux motions déposées à l'issue de l'interpellation de Mme Clémentine Barzin (MR) à la secrétaire d'État Nawal Ben Hamou sur les actions de lutte contre l'antisémitisme au regard des résolutions de 2005 et de 2023 : un ordre du jour motivé de Mme Barzin appelant à un plan bruxellois spécifique, et un ordre du jour pur et simple de M. Hasan Koyuncu (PS). Conformément à l'article 119.7 du règlement, l'ordre du jour pur et simple a la priorité de droit. Le débat a opposé ceux qui estiment que l'antisémitisme, en raison de ses racines historiques singulières et de ses manifestations propres, requiert une approche distincte, et ceux qui privilégient un cadre global de lutte antiraciste, jugeant la résolution d'octobre 2023 déjà adoptée suffisamment ciblée.
